newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Stals gloomy on rate cut prospect - paper.
newsitem.headline: S.African Stals gloomy on rate cut prospect - paper.

text.p: South African Reserve (central) Bank governor Chris Stals said at the weekend he was not confident of a cut in interest rates next year.
Stals told the Afrikaans Beeld newspaper in an interview that interest rates would either stay at their present levels or increase.
He said economists predicting rate cuts next year were wrong, the paper quoted him as saying.
"It is an optimistic view. I do not believe that interest rates would drop.
"It looks as if interest rates would remain at present levels or increase -- that is the reality," Stals said in the interview published on Monday.
Stals' comments came as the South African rand plunged further against the dollar and British pound in early Monday trade.

The currency was hit on Friday by downbeat comments by Stals at a conference where he warned the central bank might need to tighten monetary policy if there was no sign of a slowdown in bank credit extension and money supply growth.
On Monday the rand, hit by speculative selling out of London, fell to an all-time low against the dollar of 4.6430/80 after settling at 4.6110/6160 on Friday.
Stals told the newspaper he believed that the growth in money supply and granting of credit had reached a high and would decrease by the end of 1997.
"I expect that the growth in the money supply would bottom out at about 10 percent and that the growth in the granting of credit had reached its highest level," Stals said.

Preliminary figures released by the Reserve Bank on Friday showed that South Africa's year-on-year broadly defined M3 money supply grew 14.45 percent in September from August's revised 15.40 percent. Private credit expanded by 17.94 percent from 17.70.
Commercial banks' prime lending rate currently stands at 19.25 percent. The Bank rate is fixed at 16.00 percent.
